headline: BYD Stalled, Proton Shielded, B40 Priced Out: Who Wins?
context: MITI's conditions for BYD's Tanjung Malim EV plant (80% export and an RM200K price floor) stalled the world's largest EV maker's Malaysia plans, shielding Proton (49.9% Geely) and Perodua (25% Daihatsu) and pricing B40 out of the EV transition.

changes.summary: Correction: this card gave RM4,588 as the B40 median income, which is DOSM's rural median household income, and an RM100K Dolphin price our sources did not support; it now sets MITI's RM200K floor against BYD's cheaper imports.

Correction: we said BYD walked away and that Thailand set no conditions, but BYD's Tanjung Malim plans had stalled at the time and Thailand required EV makers to offset imports with local production; we also add BYD's September 2026 decision to drop the plant and correct Daihatsu's Perodua stake to 25%.

cards.big: MITI set an RM200K floor and an 80% export rule. BYD's Tanjung Malim plan stalled. In Thailand, BYD opened a plant in 2024.
cards.sub: Proton (49.9% Geely) and Perodua (25% Daihatsu) stay shielded. In Sep 2026 BYD dropped the plant, citing a change in strategy; it is in advanced talks on local assembly.

cards.big: MITI's rule puts any Tanjung Malim-built BYD sold here above RM200K. BYD's imported Dolphin and Atto 3 already sell for less.
cards.sub: AutoBuzz said the floor effectively cordons off the affordable segment. MITI has also set an RM250K floor for fully imported EVs from new brands.

cards.big: Proton had 43 years of tariffs and subsidies. It still can't compete on price.
cards.sub: Every party (BN, PH, PN) has extended the wall. 700,000 jobs includes 53,000 aftermarket shops.

cards.big: Thailand set conditions too: EV makers on its subsidy scheme had to build one car locally for each import in 2024. BYD's Thai plant opened that July.
cards.sub: The ratio rose to 1.5 in 2025; Thailand's next scheme asks 2 in 2026 and 3 in 2027. Its terms tie incentives to local output, on a timetable.

cards.big: After 43 years of protection and zero exit plan, who is the wall actually for?
Like building a wall around a garden that stopped growing 20 years ago. The wall keeps competitors out, but it also keeps the garden from getting sunlight.
cards.sub: 43 years of tariff protection have not produced a globally competitive national car; they have produced higher prices for everyone else

cards.big: 700,000 jobs deserve an honest transition, not an indefinite regressive tax on the bottom 40%.
